clue.text: Recurring sounds of wind and castanets are heard

indicators.note: are heard tells us the sounds named are to be spoken, giving letters that match their pronunciation

parts.note: wind makes a sigh and castanets make a click; said together these noises give the run of letters

explanation.surface: Something repeats: the noise of wind and the rattle of castanets keep coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGH (what wind does) plus CLICK (what castanets do), said together, gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring comes round again and again in cycles, which is what the adjective describes.

indicators.note: made in the sense of made into something else, so the letters of the two words are refashioned

explanation.surface: A tribute of mine is turned into a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' asks for the letters of MY TRIBUTE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ytterbium is a rare-earth metallic chemical element, named after the Swedish village Ytterby.

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: Someone abstains from food while eating an Italian lentil dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is an edible seed of the pea family, and such seeds are called pulses.

clue.text: Coach horse to take most of risk on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside places the shortened word for risk around the word for horse
most of drops the final letter of the word for risk

parts.note: a chance is a risk
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A coach horse is made to take a gamble by running wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final E, and 'on the outside' puts the shortened risk round the horse. A charabanc is an old-fashioned motor coach for outings.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an early open motor coach used for excursions, so it is a kind of coach.

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for skier is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket and tennis a skier is a ball hit high, a lob
to have a shy is to have a try or attempt

explanation.surface: A clumsy skier is just about to have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skier' is not a person on snow but a high-hit ball, a LOB; 'about' turns it to BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for being uncooperative or bloody-minded, i.e. deliberately awkward.

indicators.note: that's about means the word for interdiction goes round the next word

parts.note: an interdiction is a ban
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prohibition that is about to stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's.

clue.text: Important event when dead man's head is found in Scottish town

indicators.note: is found in places the abbreviation and the initial inside the town's name

parts.note: Lanark is a town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of the word man

explanation.surface: A dead man's head turns up in a Scottish town, a notable occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: D plus M (head of 'man') go inside LANARK, a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a turning point or milestone, an event of great importance.

definitions.meaning: a pony is a small equine animal

explanation.definitionFit: Both heroin in drug slang and a small equine animal share the same five-letter word.

clue.text: Turned one large seed into vegetable plant

indicators.note: into means the turned pieces are put inside the vegetable

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: turned means the following words are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nut is a large hard-shelled seed

explanation.surface: Someone turns a large seed into a vegetable plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' gives TUNI, which 'into' sets after the vegetable's E. 'vegetable plant' looks like one phrase, but plant alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a garden plant grown for its trumpet-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Type of meal that was insipid, according to Spooner

indicators.note: according to Spooner tells us to swap the opening letters of two words

parts.note: something insipid lacked punch
the second word of the phrase lacked punch

explanation.surface: A meal is described as bland by the famously muddled Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letters of LACKED PUNCH. Spooner was an Oxford don known for swapping the starts of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is a meal of sandwiches and snacks prepared to take to school or work.

clue.text: Jousting tournament doesn't include one pet

indicators.note: jousting suggests a tumbling melee, so the letters of tournament are thrown about

explanation.surface: A jousting tournament leaves out one person's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't include' strips the second word's letters before 'Jousting' rearranges the rest. 'pet' is a sulk or fit of temper, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a fit of sulking or bad temper, so a tantrum is one.

clue.text: Teams recipe for developing outstanding performance

indicators.note: developing means the letters grow into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Teams follow a recipe in order to produce a great show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for developing' asks for TEAMS and RECIPE to be rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is a work of outstanding skill, so a brilliant performance can be called one.

parts.note: one, two and so on are counting numbers, as opposed to the ordinal forms first and second

explanation.surface: Counting one, two, but refusing to say first and second.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting numbers such as one and two are distinguished from ordinals like first and second.

indicators.note: behind places the word it after the word for once

parts.note: ex means former or once
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old instruction to leave something behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or leave, a synonym.

parts.note: string players suggests violinists, but this is a pattern of string looped over the fingers in a children's game

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement for violinists and cellists.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's game of looping string over fingers to form patterns is an arrangement of string.

parts.note: read not as a significant piece of research but as the study of meaning in language

explanation.surface: A significant piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the branch of linguistics dealing with the meaning of words and sentences.

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling food
neat can mean elegant or tidy
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Describe a food shop's stylish feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to describe or portray something precisely.

clue.text: Sources of energy arising around the queen's harem

indicators.note: around has the turned fuels enclose the queen's abbreviation
arising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the words are reversed

parts.note: oil is a source of energy
gas is another source of energy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Fuel supplies come up around the queen's harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns the two fuels to SAGLIO, and 'around' sets the queen's cipher in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim palace, the harem.

clue.text: Where woodmen stay is light brown and cold inside

indicators.note: inside places the colour and the abbreviation within the word for light

parts.note: a lamp is a light
umber is a brown earth pigment
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A woodsmen's lodge has light brown walls and a chilly interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light brown' reads as one shade, but light is LAMP and brown is UMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumber camp is a settlement where loggers live while felling trees.

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for friends is reversed

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Friends blow over, like a passing storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a blow with the open hand.

indicators.note: holding means the word for hate contains the abbreviation

parts.note: spite is malice or hatred

explanation.surface: Hatred holds a mischievous royal child.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a fairy or elf, a mischievous imp-like creature.

parts.note: before decimalisation nine old pence equalled 3.75 new pence, and an old saying for being nearly exact compared things to that sum

explanation.surface: An amount almost equal to three and three-quarter pence in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's old pennies were 240 to the pound; nine of them equal 3.75 new pence, so the phrase meaning 'very close' fits the sum literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The old idiom 'as near as ninepence' means almost exactly, very close.

clue.text: Stood by any other name from Shakespeare?

definitions.meaning: stood as in got up from sitting

definitions.text: by any other name from Shakespeare?
definitions.meaning: completes Juliet's line about a flower that would smell as sweet whatever it was called

explanation.definitionFit: Got up is the past of rise, and a flower 'by any other name' comes from Romeo and Juliet.

indicators.note: in places the word for mother inside the word for tacit agreement

parts.note: a nod is agreement given without words
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A traveller's mother gives a silent nod of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home, a traveller.

clue.text: Crook causing stink about piles with quarters missing

indicators.note: about means the word for stink surrounds the other piece

parts.note: hum is slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: quarters are compass points, so two of those letters are removed

parts.note: oodles means piles or lots

explanation.surface: A villain creates a stench by sitting on heaps with no rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' are compass points, here E and S; 'about' wraps the trimmed piles in the stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a gangster or thug, a crook.

clue.text: One couple takes it to reproduce

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: takes means the word for couple contains the following word

parts.note: to mate is to couple or pair

explanation.surface: One couple takes on a project to reproduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy, which is to reproduce something.

definitions.meaning: to back a motion is to support it formally
a jiffy is a very short moment

explanation.definitionFit: To support a proposal formally, or a brief instant of time, are both senses of the word.

indicators.note: holding means the word for sinkhole contains the abbreviation

parts.note: a sewer is a drain or sinkhole for waste
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A drain contains the king's saliva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit' is not saliva but a rod for roasting meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a long rod on which meat is roasted, and a skewer is such a rod.
